perspective:
From Carolyn Abebe’s perspective, she knows/experienced the following:

- Carolyn works with Marilyn Olson at a community bank and has recently started getting to know her as a colleague.
- During a busy, stressful week with increased customer traffic, Carolyn noticed Marilyn was unusually quiet and withdrawn compared with her normally engaging demeanor. Carolyn asked if everything was alright and whether Marilyn wanted to talk. Marilyn said she was overwhelmed by work and some personal stuff, and thanked Carolyn for asking.
- In a later interaction, Carolyn experienced Marilyn as curt. This confused and slightly hurt Carolyn. Carolyn told Marilyn she hoped she hadn’t overstepped, shared that she had also had tough times, and said talking can sometimes help. Marilyn said she appreciated it, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week.
- After that, Marilyn appeared to Carolyn to respond positively to her openness. Carolyn felt relieved and hopeful. Carolyn invited Marilyn to a small weekend get-together with friends. Marilyn said it sounded lovely, thanked her, and said she would love to join.
- Despite friendly interactions outside work, Carolyn perceived Marilyn as still maintaining a professional distance at the bank. Carolyn felt disappointed and asked to talk about their work dynamic, saying she felt a distance she couldn’t understand. Marilyn said she hadn’t realized it, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed to talk about improving collaboration.
- After their private meeting, Carolyn believed they had cleared the air and better understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries. She felt content and optimistic. Carolyn proposed teaming up for the new project proposal. Marilyn said that was a great idea, was glad they had talked, and looked forward to working more closely with Carolyn.

Carolyn does not have access to Marilyn’s private thoughts, unspoken feelings, or reasons beyond what Marilyn stated or what Carolyn observed/perceived.
